title: Ashes or sand? John Arcilla goes to NBI to check pets' remains in wake of dumped carcasses in Bulacan
summary: Actor John Arcilla went to the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) on Wednesday to seek the bureau"s help in authenticating the ashes of two of his pets. Arcilla made the move weeks after the…

blocks.text: Actor John Arcilla went to the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) on Wednesday to seek the bureau’s help in authenticating the ashes of two of his pets.
Arcilla made the move weeks after the remains of more than 20 dogs and cats were found dumped along a road in Bulacan. Authorities discovered that the carcasses were supposed to have been cremated.

“Iniisip ko kung nangyari ‘yon sa Bulacan, sandali lang, ito bang kini-keep ko ang ilang taon na to… baka mamaya sand lang to? Anong klaseng ash lang to? So gusto kong ipa-check dito sa NBI,” Arcilla told reporters.
(I was thinking, if that happened in Bulacan, wait a minute—what I’ve been keeping all these years, could this just be sand? What kind of ash is this? So I wanted to have it checked here at the NBI.)

He clarified that he did not avail himself of the services of Ahjay Paws Aftercare Pet Crematorium in Bacoor City, Cavite, which is currently being investigated for allegedly dumping the remains found in Bulacan.

The actor shared that 12 of his pets were cremated across different crematoriums, and even though he has kept their urns for nearly a decade, he grew paranoid that the ashes of the animals, whom he considers family, might not be real either.

“Kasi magmula nung nangyari yung sa Bulacan, bigla kang nagkaroon ng paranoia na—kasi 12 na kasi yung dogs ko na pina-cremate ko pero tatlong crematorium.. Ayokong i-divulge ‘yung name yet kasi hindi pa naman ako sure, kaya lang gusto ko lang kasing ma-sure na yung ashes na nasa akin [ay sila talaga],” Arcilla said.

(Because ever since what happened in Bulacan, you suddenly get paranoid—I’ve had 12 dogs cremated across three crematoriums. I don’t want to divulge the names yet because I’m not sure, I just want to be certain that the ashes in my possession are really theirs.)
He shared that it took him a while before deciding to have the ashes of his departed pets tested, as he did not know how he would feel if the results turned out negative.
However, the actor stressed that he also felt a responsibility to find out whether the cremation services he availed were legitimate so he could warn future clients if they were not.

“Kasi mamaya yung resulta hindi ko gusto, anong mararamdaman ko? Anong gagawin ko doon sa aking isang sacred space a 12 yung family member ko na anandoon tapos kini-keep ko ng almost a decade na and wala na akong balak na itapon sya kasi hindi naman yon basura eh,” Arcilla said.

(What if the results aren’t what I want, how will I feel? What will I do with that sacred space of mine where my 12 family members are kept, which I’ve maintained for nearly a decade and have no intention of throwing away because they aren’t trash?)
“Pag napatunayan kong hindi pala totoo yon, edi i have to save the other clients of that pet crematorium,” he added.
(If I prove that they aren’t real, then I have to save the other clients of that pet crematorium.)

Last week, the NBI found that the urns provided to pet owners by the controversial Cavite pet crematorium did not contain animal remains, prompting several owners to file complaints before the Department of Justice.
Its owners and other individuals involved now face charges of estafa and violations of the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act. —NB, GMA News
